name: small-business-rescue-bakery
title: The Last Croissant
note: The founder-approved v9 story. Its rough cut was drafted in Google Flow with the same arc (docs/examples).

cast.owner: the baker in round glasses and a yellow headscarf
cast.rival: the blond influencer in a gold puffer vest
cast.regular: the cheerful old man in a flat cap and a green cardigan
cast.hero1: the muscular bearded man with wavy dark hair in a black t-shirt with thin green stripes
cast.hero2: the muscular man with short curly dark hair and a thin moustache in a plain black t-shirt

slots.place: the small cozy family bakery with a striped awning
slots.rival_place: gold mega-bakery with a giant inflatable bun on the roof
slots.busy: Customers queue with paper bags of warm croissants while fresh trays fill the display case.
slots.unsold: A full tray of unsold croissants sits in the display case.
slots.count_line: Six. We sold six croissants today.
slots.regular_line: Best croissants in town, Rosa! Don't you ever change.
slots.offer_item: A single golden croissant sits alone on the counter, in plain view.
slots.offer_action: slides the last croissant across the counter toward them and says kindly
slots.taste_setup: {hero1} holds the last croissant, about to bite; {hero2} stands beside, curious.
slots.taste: bites the croissant: a loud flaky crunch, flakes everywhere; a silent stunned beat, mouth closed while chewing
slots.bad_idea_line: Okay. Ideas. A dancing croissant mascot? Free gold croissants?
slots.good_idea_line: ...No. This should have a line around the block.
slots.heirloom: a faded photo of a grandmother baking in this same bakery and a handwritten recipe card
slots.craft: folding butter into dough by hand
slots.craft_line: Don't look at us. Look at the dough.
slots.regular_back_line: Told you. They always come back.
slots.payoff: a glossy candy-red original two-seat convertible with no badges, no emblems and no plate text
